title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing traditions that define the Spartan experience at Aurora University, from historic fundraising clubs to modern cultural celebrations.

cards.title: High-Fives with Sammy Spartan
cards.subtitle: The Face of Spartan Pride
cards.notes: Look for Sammy Spartan leading the Homecoming Parade and rallying the crowd at Vago Field. Students often snap photos with him during major campus events and National Mascot Day.
cards.short_summary: Sammy Spartan is the official mascot of Aurora University, appearing at athletic contests and community celebrations to foster school spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Sammy Spartan is the official mascot of Aurora University and leads the annual Homecoming Parade.
cards.access_notes: Visible at major athletic events and campus-wide celebrations like Homecoming.

cards.title: Global Flavors at Cultural Fest
cards.subtitle: A Celebration on the Quad
cards.notes: Head to the Quad in late September to sample international cuisine and watch cultural performances. Students host booths featuring traditional arts, crafts, and games.
cards.short_summary: Cultural Fest is an annual event on the University Quad that celebrates the diverse backgrounds of the AU community through food, music, and art.
cards.evidence_claim: The Annual Cultural Fest takes place on the Aurora University Quad and features international cuisine, arts, and performances.
cards.access_notes: Open to the campus community; typically held in the afternoon on the main Quad.

cards.title: Giving Back on April 4
cards.subtitle: Commemorating the Move to Aurora
cards.notes: Participate in this 24-hour giving event held every April 4th. It marks the anniversary of the university's 1912 move from Mendota to its current Aurora campus.
cards.short_summary: The Day of Generosity is an annual fundraising and community event held on April 4 to celebrate the university's history and support student initiatives.
cards.evidence_claim: The first-ever Day of Generosity took place on April 4, 2025, marking the anniversary of classes beginning at the Aurora campus in 1912.
cards.access_notes: A virtual and campus-wide event held annually on April 4.

cards.title: Legacy of the Tin Can Jimmie Club
cards.subtitle: A Century of Student Support
cards.notes: Learn about this historic club founded in 1912 to raise the university's first endowment. Its legacy of student-led philanthropy continues to be taught in campus history tours.
cards.short_summary: Founded in 1912, the Tin Can Jimmie Club was a student organization dedicated to raising funds for the college's endowment during its early years in Aurora.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tin Can Jimmie Club was formed in 1912 to raise funds for the college endowment.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition referenced in university archives and timeline.

cards.title: The Official Spartan Welcome
cards.subtitle: Kicking Off Welcome Week
cards.notes: Join your fellow freshmen for this formal induction into the Spartan family. It features campus spirit rallies and introductions to university leadership.
cards.short_summary: Welcome Convocation is the official opening ceremony for new students during Welcome Week, designed to build community and school pride.
cards.evidence_claim: Welcome Convocation kicks off Welcome Week with campus spirit and an official welcome to the Spartan family.
cards.access_notes: Required for all incoming first-year students during the fall semester.

cards.title: Culture for the Community
cards.subtitle: A Public Lecture and Performance Series
cards.notes: Attend free lectures and performances in Crimi Auditorium. This series brings world-class thinkers and artists to campus for the benefit of students and the public.
cards.short_summary: Celebrating Arts and Ideas is a long-standing cultural series at AU that offers free music, theatre, and guest lectures to the university and local community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Celebrating Arts and Ideas series offers unique cultural experiences, free of charge, to the university community.
cards.access_notes: Events are typically held in Crimi Auditorium and are open to the public.

cards.title: Dialogue at the Wackerlin Center
cards.subtitle: Monthly Identity Discussions
cards.notes: Join a monthly discussion series focused on identity and culture. These sessions encourage students to share perspectives and engage in meaningful dialogue.
cards.short_summary: Cultural Exchange is a monthly discussion series hosted by the Wackerlin Center that focuses on identity, culture, and social justice.
cards.evidence_claim: Cultural Exchange is a monthly diversity discussion series focused on identity and culture hosted by the Wackerlin Center.
cards.access_notes: Held monthly at the Wackerlin Center or designated campus rooms.

cards.title: The Walk to Vago Field
cards.subtitle: A Game Day Rite of Passage
cards.notes: Line the path to Vago Field to cheer on the football team as they make their traditional walk to the stadium before home games.
cards.short_summary: The Spartan Walk is a pre-game tradition where the football team marches to the stadium, accompanied by fans and the pep band.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spartan Walk is a documented tradition for the Aurora University football team on game days.
cards.access_notes: Occurs before home football games; fans gather along the route to the field.

cards.title: Winter Break Reflection
cards.subtitle: A New Year Reset
cards.notes: Sign up for this winter break retreat featuring guided reflections and trail walks. It is designed to help students start the new year refreshed and focused.
cards.short_summary: The Revive Retreat is a winter break program that offers students a chance for meditation, reflection, and community building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wackerlin Center hosts a Revive Retreat during winter break for reflection and meditation.
cards.access_notes: Requires registration; typically held in early January.

cards.title: The Graduation Pose
cards.subtitle: A Milestone Photo Op
cards.notes: Don't miss the chance to take a photo with the Spartan Statue in your graduation regalia. It is a quintessential rite of passage for every AU graduate.
cards.short_summary: The Spartan Statue is a central campus landmark where students and alumni gather for photos, especially during Commencement and Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spartan Statue is a key location for student and alumni photos during traditions like Homecoming and Commencement.
cards.access_notes: Accessible year-round on the main campus grounds.
